office_does: The three Clallam County commissioners hold the county's legislative and executive power: they adopt the budget and ordinances, levy taxes, adopt the comprehensive plan and oversee county departments. They are nominated by district and elected countywide.
race_blurb: First-term incumbent Mike French (Prefers Democratic Party) faces first-time candidate Jake Seegers (Prefers Independent Party), who led the District 3 primary 52.7% to 47.1%. All county voters choose in November. The two differ most on harm reduction and homelessness, taxes and fees, land use, and climate policy.

candidates.summary: Port Angeles investment consultant and real estate investor making his first run for office, on public safety, economic development, affordability and asking of every program 'Is it essential? Is it effective?'
highlights: Pledges to grow county revenue 'without increasing taxes or fees' and to reduce permit fees [S3][S13]
Says the county is 'enabling' with harm reduction; favors a one-for-one syringe exchange and transitional over permanent supportive housing [S13]
Says the state has restricted property rights and land use 'far beyond what is necessary' and the county should not add to it [S17]
Led the District 3 primary with 52.7% of the vote [S7]
PDC found a violation over blog sponsor identification; $250 penalty suspended on conditions [S14]

taxes.basis: Repeated pledges to fund priorities without raising taxes or fees, to lower fees, and to back a new sales tax only if another ends.

spending.basis: Runs on restoring budget oversight and testing every program for whether it is essential and effective; criticizes 'more grants, more government spending and more money to NGOs.'

housing.basis: Wants lower permit fees, pushback on state mandates, and land use left to property owners; favors transitional over permanent supportive housing.

safety.basis: Calls public safety his top priority. Supports OPNET and equipping officers to address encampments, says the county's harm reduction is 'enabling,' and wants recovery measured as an outcome; also backs co-response programs.

climate.basis: Says the county climate vulnerability assessment uses extreme assumptions and was not required, and opposes carbon-credit-only management that would stop timber harvests; no broader energy-policy statements.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience, running to change the 'culture of county government.'

candidates.summary: First-term District 3 commissioner and former Port Angeles City Councilmember and downtown business owner, running on economic development (he led the $35.6 million Recompete effort), housing, public safety and climate.
highlights: Chaired the coalition that won $35.6 million in federal Recompete funds for jobs and workforce training [S1][S5]
Pushed for the local 0.1% affordable-housing sales tax, now about $1.5 million a year countywide [S6][S18]
Supports harm reduction alongside treatment and law enforcement; backs co-response, OPNET and more sheriff positions on the sheriff's recommendation [S7][S18]
Calls climate change 'the most important and urgent political issue of our time'; worked on the 2023 Climate Action Plan update [S8]
Describes himself as an advocate of 'conservative budgeting,' avoiding debt and protecting reserves [S1]

taxes.basis: Advanced a local affordable-housing sales tax and says he would support a county public-safety sales tax, while acknowledging voter resistance to more property tax and calling for conservative fiscal management.

spending.basis: Runs on public investment (Recompete, Opportunity Fund infrastructure, affordable-housing seed money), tempered by stated conservative budgeting and the county's 7% cut exercise.

housing.basis: Genuinely mixed: a record of deregulation (MFTE, infill SEPA exemption, ADUs, park models, fewer parking requirements) alongside public funding for affordable and permanent supportive housing.

safety.basis: Favors harm reduction, co-response, sanctioned camping and transitional housing, and says criminalizing homelessness doesn't work; also supports OPNET, more deputies and enforcing boundaries.

climate.basis: Calls climate the most urgent issue, updated the county Climate Action Plan, pushed fleet electrification and defended the climate vulnerability assessment.

experience.basis: Incumbent commissioner since 2023 after five years on the Port Angeles City Council, running on an enacted record.
